concerns.text: T028b explicitly forbids storing the full array of permutation p-values ('Do NOT store the full array... Only store the calculated KS statistic'). This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Principle IV (Single Source of Truth) because the 'Gold Standard' reference distribution cannot be independently verified or re-computed without the raw data. FR-004 requires comparing against this reference, but the task removes the evidence required to validate that comparison.

T030 mandates computing bootstrap confidence intervals for KS statistics but fails to specify that the resampling must be performed on the *permutation-based* reference distribution (the Gold Standard) rather than the standard test p-values. FR-004 and Constitution Principle VII require the KS statistic to be measured *against* the permutation reference; calculating CIs on the wrong distribution (standard vs permutation) would invalidate the 'Statistical Validity Reporting' principle and the research claim.

T011b is marked 'Superseded' and removes the power analysis task, yet SC-005 requires that the simulation iteration count achieves statistical power ≥ 0.8 to detect a KS deviation > 0.05. By removing the task that justifies the '1000 iterations' design parameter, the tasks list fails to provide the verification step required by SC-005, creating a gap in the 'Verified Accuracy' (Constitution Principle II) chain.

T043 removes the fixed KS > 0.1 threshold and asks to 'report the full range' and flag the top [deferred] of deviations. This weakens FR-007 (Sensitivity Analysis) and SC-001 by failing to define a concrete, testable acceptance criterion for what constitutes a 'high deviation' or 'failure mode'. Without a defined threshold or metric for the 'top [deferred]', the task cannot be verified against the spec's requirement to 'quantify the degree of anti-conservative bias'.

T028a relies on T019e (Deterministic RNG Wrapper) to 'regenerate' the matrix for the permutation test. Constitution Principle VI (Simulation Fidelity) mandates that synthetic datasets be created using specific correlation matrices and seeds recorded in metadata. Relying on a wrapper to re-seed the RNG risks bit-for-bit drift if the wrapper does not perfectly replicate the original generation sequence, violating the 'Single Source of Truth' for the specific data instance being tested against the Gold Standard.
